text:
Just finished reading this fascinating little book. 

J. Paul Getty wrote a series of 19 essays for Playboy magazine back in the 1960s. His goal was to transfer what he learned in his 50 year career to younger businessmen. 

His main advice is: 

1. You’re too focused on speculating and trading. The best entrepreneurs don’t want to trade, they want to own. They know all the real money is in the long term. Most people are too impatient and incompetent to understand that. 

An example he uses in the book: a young man buys an oil lease on Monday for $4,000. He sell it to Getty on Tuesday for $8,000. The young man is bragging about doubling his money in 24 hours. Getty makes $800,000 on that lease over the next decade. 

2.  If all the real money is in the long term then your business needs to be optimized for survival. Keep a lot of cash, invest in technology that makes your business more efficient, watch your costs 24/7, be careful with debt, and be on site where the work happens. 

3.  Don’t panic over problems. The perfect business does not exist. There are always problems in every business all the time. 

This is one of my favorite lines in the book: 

“The truly great leader views reverses calmly and coolly. He is fully aware that they are bound to occur occasionally and refuses to be unnerved by them.”

4.  The worst thing that can happen to an entrepreneur is to become structured and homogenized. Getty knew all the top entrepreneurs of his day and they all made their biggest success by bucking conventional wisdom. They found opportunity in ideas other people rejected or ignored as impossible. 

Another great line from the book: 

“You’ll go much further if you stop trying to look and act and think like everyone else.” 

5.  Optimism is a moral duty. Pessimism aborts opportunity. 

Young people would tell Getty that all the good opportunities are gone. That they are too late. That you can’t build a business and make a fortune today. That it is no longer possible. (They said this in 1965!)

Getty’s believed there’s always opportunity because a business is just an idea that makes someone else’s life better and there’s unlimited ways to do so. 
—
There’s a lot more in the book. It’s easy to read. You can also listen to the podcast I made about the book (episode 353)

text:
5 Essential Tips for Career Success in 2025

Below are five actionable pieces of advice to help you succeed in your career in 2025!

1 - Master the Art of Networking:
Networking isn't just about collecting contacts; it's about building meaningful relationships. Attend industry events, join professional groups, and engage on platforms like LinkedIn. Remember, it's not just about who you know but how well you maintain those connections. 

Action: Attend at least one networking event per month and follow up with new contacts within 48 hours.

2 - Keep Learning:

The job market evolves rapidly. Staying relevant means continuous learning. Whether it's through online courses, certifications, or workshops, investing in your skills is investing in your career. 

Action: Enrol in one new course or certification related to your field.

3 - Tailor Your Resume:

A one-size-fits-all resume won't cut it. Customise your resume for each job application, focusing on how your experiences align with the job description. Use keywords from the job posting to pass ATS (Applicant Tracking Systems).

Action: Before applying, spend 15 minutes tailoring your resume to match the job requirements.

4 - Embrace Soft Skills: 

Technical skills are vital, but soft skills like communication, teamwork, and problem-solving are what make you irreplaceable. 

Action: Seek feedback on your soft skills from colleagues or mentors and work on one area of improvement each month.

5 - Navigate Career Transitions:

Changing careers or industries can be daunting but rewarding. Start by identifying transferable skills, then seek out informational interviews in your target field to bridge the knowledge gap.

Action: Reach out to someone in your desired industry for a 15-minute informational interview this week.

🔥 Bonus Tip: Don't underestimate the power of a personal project or side hustle. It can showcase your initiative, passion, and skills in a practical context.
